assumptions.choice: The average ATR over 50 bars is a 50-period simple moving average of ATR(14).
assumptions.reason: The specification says average ATR value but does not name a smoothing method.

assumptions.choice: An EMA is sloping up when its current value exceeds its prior-bar value, and sloping down when it is below its prior-bar value.
assumptions.reason: No numerical angle or slope lookback is specified.

assumptions.choice: Only high-volatility conditions satisfying both EMA direction and relative-position requirements are Segment 2 or Segment 3; all other high-volatility states are non-tradable neutral states.
assumptions.reason: The detailed Segment 2 and Segment 3 definitions require both EMA relationships and matching slopes.

assumptions.choice: The bar enters the EMA zone when its high-low range overlaps the interval between EMA(20) and EMA(50); a long pullback requires a lower close than the prior bar and a short pullback requires a higher close.
assumptions.reason: The specification does not define an intrabar touch rule or a pullback direction measurement.

assumptions.choice: A bullish pin bar has a positive body, lower wick at least twice the body, and upper wick no larger than the body; bearish is the mirrored condition.
Longs require EMA(200) to slope up and shorts require EMA(200) to slope down.
assumptions.reason: This applies the stated prohibition against trading against the EMA(200) global trend.

assumptions.choice: Position size is floor(1% of current broker equity divided by 2 ATR), excluding commissions from the stop-loss risk calculation.
assumptions.reason: The specification defines maximum loss by stop distance but does not state whether commissions are included or how fractional shares are handled.

assumptions.choice: Stop-loss and take-profit orders are submitted after the entry order completes, using its actual execution price and ATR captured when the entry was signaled.
assumptions.reason: The actual entry price is not known until order execution in Backtrader.
